quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when the roads are wet.
Use tires with proper air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your car slides on a thin layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights, but it has a crossbuck sign. You should:

options.text: Approach all tracks with extreme caution and cross only when you know there is no train coming.
Turn your radio down so you can listen for an approaching train.
Only continue when a flagger tells you it is safe to cross.

questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: When can you turn left with the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: A solid green arrow means you can go in the direction it points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before you brake.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop in time. Release the accelerator to slow your car. Then apply steady brake pressure to stop smoothly.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is safest?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than the other cars.
Drive slower than the other cars.
Drive at the same speed as the other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as the other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars. Drive with the flow of traffic while staying within the speed limit.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When you see a child about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when you think someone does not see you. For example, honk if a child is about to run in front of your car.

questions.question: Highways and roads freeze before ramps and bridges.
questions.explanation: Ramps and bridges hang in the air and freeze faster than regular roads in cold weather. Drive slowly and carefully when crossing bridges in freezing conditions.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving does not increase your crash risk much.
questions.explanation: Using a phone while driving distracts you and increases your crash risk.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, you should start from:
questions.explanation: When turning left from a multilane street or highway, start from the left lane.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A "reduced speed" sign tells you to slow down. When a new speed limit is shown on this sign, that speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition with proper tread.
Keep your tires inflated to the correct pressure.
Drive slower when it is raining.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, you should: keep your tires in good condition with proper tread, keep them inflated to the correct pressure, and drive slower in the rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road curves back and forth. Slow down to drive safely through the curves.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes on an interstate. Do not stop on the shoulder unless it is an emergency. Change lanes only when necessary. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: A traffic light shows a green arrow and a red light. What does this mean?

options.text: You can only drive straight ahead.
You can only drive in the direction the green arrow points.
You must wait for a solid green light to go in any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction the green arrow points.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow appears with a red light, you can only drive in the direction of the arrow. Make sure the intersection is clear before you proceed.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees you.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
Give pedestrians the right-of-way only when they have the legal right.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian. It is your responsibility to watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way at all times, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line down the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: The road has traffic moving in both directions.
The road has traffic moving in only one direction.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road has traffic moving in both directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, what should you use to show you are turning?
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show when you plan to turn.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what lights should you use?

options.text: It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves to the right and then to the left. Slow down so you can safely handle these curves.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when visibility is 500 feet or less. Use low beams in fog. High beams reflect light back into your eyes and make it harder to see.

questions.question: It starts raining while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive close behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: When it rains heavily, slow down and turn on your headlights. If you cannot see clearly, pull over and wait for the rain to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign prevent?

options.text: Entry from the wrong direction on one-way streets and freeway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entry from the wrong direction on one-way streets and freeway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic flows in one direction only. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of moving traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of moving traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal before merging and match the speed of traffic on the freeway. Always yield to other vehicles when entering.

questions.question: What should drivers do when turning left?

options.text: Slow down gradually and check your rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Signal 3 to 5 seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. Move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.
